subject: SLA combo pack vs a-la-carte — pricing & packaging breakdown
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@skylinehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@skylinehealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA combo pack vs a-la-carte — request for pricing breakdown

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking a look at our RFP. We're evaluating two approaches for operational support and SLA coverage:

1) A bundled 'combo' SLA package that combines uptime guarantees, a retainer-based oncall response, and an escalation playbook (one SKU).
2) A-la-carte add-ons where we pick uptime tier, response windows, and pay incident/retainer separately.

Can you provide a concise comparison for both options (pricing bands, example cost at 75M tokens/month, any one-time onboarding fees, and how regional failover affects pricing)? We're on a procurement cadence and need a short write-up + sample SOW by COB next Tuesday (2027-10-12).

I've attached our RFP table for context. Also flag any gating security requirements (SOC2 artifacts, audit log retention) we should include up front.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Director, Cloud Operations
Skyline Health

Attachment: Skyline_SLA_RFP_20271010.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA combo pack vs a-la-carte — request for pricing breakdown

Hi Priya — thanks for the RFP, that makes the ask clear. Quick clarifying questions before we build the comparison:

- Is the 75M tokens/month an average or a committed minimum? Any seasonal peaks (daily/weekly)?
- Do you require cross-region active-active failover or cold standby (failover window)?
- Are there specific retention windows for audit logs beyond 90 days?

High-level guidance up front:
- Combo pack: lower blended unit cost, includes a monthly retainer (24/7 oncall for P1/P0), and gives predictable unit economics. Ideal if you want a single invoice and fewer purchase orders.
- A-la-carte: more flexible, can save if you expect few incidents. Larger per-incident / per-hour charges and less amortized retainer.

I'll loop Kimberley for the detailed cost model and a quick two-sheet deliverable: one tab with combo pricing, one with a-la-carte permutations. Expect a first draft within 24 hours after we confirm commitment assumptions.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA combo pack vs a-la-carte — request for pricing breakdown

Hi Mateo,

Answers below:
- 75M tokens/month is our committed baseline for FY28. We expect a seasonal uplift (~20%) in Q4.
- We need active-active failover across us-west and eu-west regions; RTO target for control-plane failures is 15 minutes for critical endpoints, 1 hour for non-critical.
- Audit logs: 365 days preferred, some compliance teams may ask for 7 years on specific endpoints (we can flag those later).

Procurement timeline: 6 weeks to contract signature after pricing acceptance; pilot can start earlier.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Shah
Director, Cloud Operations
Skyline Health

Attachment: Skyline_procurement_requirements_20271011.pdf (PDF)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@skylinehealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-11T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA combo pack vs a-la-carte — request for pricing breakdown

Hi Priya / Mateo — attaching a compact comparison and a sample pricing table (combo vs a-la-carte) tuned to the 75M committed baseline. Key summary here inline so you don't have to open the sheet: 

Summary (75M tokens / mo, active-active us-west + eu-west):

Option A — Combo SLA Pack (recommended for Skyline if you want predictability):
- Uptime: 99.95% (monthly availability credits per SLA)
- Included: 24/7 retainer (P0/P1 triage + primary engineer + escalation manager), quarterly DR runbooks, SOC2 evidence access, 365d audit-log retention for primary endpoints.
- One-time onboarding: $45,000 (runbooks, DR validation, KMS integration assistance).
- Monthly recurring: Base serving + SLA combo fee. At 75M tokens this equals approx $68k/mo blended (includes amortized retainer).
- Discount: 15% off list if you sign a 12-month commit and prepay 6 months.

Option B — A-la-carte (flexible, lower upfront):
- Picked pieces: uptime tier (99.9% / 99.95%), optional retainer (hourly billed incidents + optional retainer), ad-hoc DR exercises.
- One-time onboarding: $18,000.
- Example monthly: Base serving + incident credit pool + optional retainer. For 75M tokens, approx $74k/mo if you do not purchase the retainer and assume 2 P0s/year.

Tradeoffs: combo reduces volatility and procurement overhead (single SKU + single PO); a-la-carte can be cheaper if you have a mature ops team that tolerates slower response windows. Active-active failover adds ~8–12% to the monthly serving cost and a separate regional failover configuration fee (one-time) of ~$12k for runbook validation.

We can structure a 6-month pilot with a pro-rated onboarding fee if procurement requires shorter initial term. I'll outline two term options in the attached: (A) 12-month commit with 15% discount, (B) 6-month pilot + optional roll into combo pack with a credit for onboarding.

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Combo_vAla_20271011.xlsx (pricing workbook)

Let me know if you'd like this turned into an explicit SOW + cost worksheet for procurement. If so, we'll prepare a draft MSA + SOW and route it for review.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya@skylinehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@skylinehealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA combo pack vs a-la-carte — request for pricing breakdown

Kimberly — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups: 

- Procurement would prefer a 6-month pilot with an option to extend to 12 months if KPIs are met. Can you confirm the pro-rated onboarding fee for a 6-month pilot and whether the onboarding credit can be applied if we convert to 12 months?
- For escrow/audit: we require an attestation about audit-log integrity and an annual SOC2 snapshot during term. Can Redwood support 365d retention by default and offer extended retention add-on for specific endpoints?
- Legal will request a clause for escalation SLA credits; we typically ask for an escalation manager contact and a 2hr acknowledgement for P0s.

If you can send a draft MSA + SOW and call out the pilot conversion credit, we can get legal review started.

Thanks — Priya

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA combo pack vs a-la-carte — request for pricing breakdown

Priya — quick answers and next steps: 

- 6-month pilot onboarding: pro-rated onboarding fee would be $24,000 (we amortize 50% of the standard onboarding for pilots). If you convert to a 12-month committed combo pack within the pilot, we'll credit the full $24k back against the first two months of the combo pack fee.
- Audit logs: we can provide 365d retention by default for primary endpoints; extended retention (up to 7 years) available as an add-on SKU — we'll call that out in the SOW. SOC2 snapshot access is available quarterly as part of the combo pack (or on-demand for a small fee under a-la-carte).
- Escalation: we can commit to a 2hr acknowledgement for P0s and provide an escalation manager contact as part of the combo pack. 

Next steps: we'll prepare a draft MSA + 2-page SOW (pilot terms + conversion credit) and a cost worksheet tied to the 75M baseline. I'll drop the docs into HubSpot and post the DocuSign MSA link by EOD tomorrow. Can we schedule a 30-min legal + procurement sync on Thursday?
